analysis.title: Fed's Williams / Nvidia Impacts / Japan's Katayama / Microsoft Outage
key_insights: NY Fed's Williams warned US inflation is too high and the Fed needs to act over time to return it to 2%. His bias has moved from 'one more hike this year, none needed in 2027' to a gradual but continued rise in rates. He said 'the data is speaking very clearly to us — the economy is strong, labor market continues to strengthen and inflation is persistent'.
UBS Macro Sales says Williams has replaced Waller as one of Chair Warsh's two senior lieutenants for conveying the Fed's direction of travel, even though Warsh says he dislikes guidance.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stepped down effective immediately, with CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. Huang agreed to testify before Congress before Thanksgiving. UBS analyst Timothy Arcuri (Nov 11, before the departure was confirmed) said the impact would be felt far and wide because Nvidia funds neo-clouds, LLM developers, ecosystem partners and suppliers, and expects a 'pause' in its willingness to pursue those deals near term.
Tighter US export restrictions could limit NVDA and AMD shipments to China and also to regions such as Singapore and Malaysia.

USDJPY broke above 160 in NY trading Thursday. Japan Finance Minister Katayama said officials will work with the US Treasury on appropriate action against one-sided, rapid moves, reviving intervention speculation.

UBS FX trading says the JPY trade-weighted index shows the USDJPY move is driven by dollar strength rather than yen weakness. With the Fed more hawkish than the BoJ and more hikes priced, any intervention would likely fail longer term because rate differentials would be unchanged or wider.

Microsoft's global outage hit Microsoft 365, Outlook and Teams for tens of thousands of users in 74 countries for more than 10 hours, still unresolved as of 10:00 London Friday. Microsoft cited 'elevated load' with no sign of a cyber attack. OpenAI and Anthropic reported issues with their Microsoft connectors. It follows an Azure outage weeks earlier.

Trump said 'We don't need a deal with Iran' and appeared to claim victory and walk away. VP Vance, who has worked back channels for a deal, was told to focus on domestic matters. The USS Theodore Roosevelt group arrives in the Gulf within days, bringing carriers to three and US personnel to about 60,000.

Kushner said the US cannot reach a Russia-Ukraine deal without Europe. Russia and Ukraine agreed to expand the next round of talks to include European partners. A speaker at the UBS European conference said the administration may push for a conclusion on Ukraine and Iran to improve Trump's legacy, and to watch for greater US urgency.

The IAEA said it cannot determine the extent of Iran's uranium stocks. It called its lack of site access 'a matter of serious proliferation' and said it cannot tell whether nuclear material was diverted to weapons research (Reuters).

UBS Australia economist Stephen Wu expects October headline CPI at 4.7% y/y, a new cycle high, from 4.3% in September (no consensus yet), with 0.3% m/m driven by fuel (about 24bp) and the card surcharging ban from Oct 1. He sees this as the peak, the first RBA cut in November 2027 and a shallow 50bp cycle, with risks tilting toward earlier and/or larger easing.

The White House is discussing ousting Commerce Secretary Lutnick amid the Chinese spy controversy around Huang and criticism over not adding dozens of Chinese firms to the trade blacklist and over Nvidia China export oversight (Reuters).

OpenAI backs a bipartisan Congressional effort to block China's access to AI chips and chipmaking equipment (Bloomberg). Three proposals would restrict future high-end chip sales, reduce diversion of Nvidia processors and block China from ASML machinery, and would be attached to annual defense legislation that must pass by year-end.

Precious metals remain a rates trade first. Gold touched 13-month lows in NY Thursday and its Asia bounce looks like short covering. UBS is tactically bearish below $3,940-4,000, with elevated speculative length and ETF outflows leaving XAU exposed if $3,860 breaks. 1M options are the cleaner expression, with implied below realised and downside skew bid.

Silver looks better than gold on a relative basis: less crowded positioning, monthly ETF creation and the structural deficit. Near-term puts remain bid. PGMs are moving with gold and silver under yield pressure, with heavy front-tenor borrowing in thin London trade. Bottom line is cautious gold, relatively constructive silver, and a dovish turn could reverse the market quickly.

UBS equity research (Nicolas Gaudois) says AI memory procurement supports undersupply and stronger profitability into 2028. Samsung is the top pick for HBM execution, DRAM pricing and shareholder returns. SK Hynix stays Buy at 1.0x 2028E book despite lower near-term pricing estimates and a possible loss of HBM leadership. A cycle peak in late 2028 or early 2029 is a risk if AI capex softens.

Rates desk trade idea: pay the AUD Z26 3s10s swap EFP box, which has flattened sharply. 10y ACGB asset swaps screen cheap to 3y as ACGB duration supply falls after the 2057 syndication and ahead of January SSA supply at the shorter end, which should steepen the box.

UBS Brazil note: fiscal progress but debt risks persist. Low vol favors downside hedges onshore, equity dispersion rises, offshore outflows persist with some value interest, BRL downside is increasingly priced, front-end FX vol favors steepeners. DeMark technicals are bearish USDBRL and bullish Bovespa.

FX flows Thursday were modest USD selling, mainly versus EUR, AUD and JPY, read as profit taking. The desk does not see long USD positioning as crowded and expects room to add, with the market awaiting data validation of Waller and Logan's hawkishness. EURUSD resistance is 1.1100/1.1110, then 1.1160/70.

Europe credit: 5 new issues Thursday. Two SSA deals landed at IPT with weak demand. Three covered bonds tightened 7bp versus IPT with good demand, one Italian deal still landing with decent NIP. Secondary sub-5y covered bonds saw two-way flow, with bids firming in French covered and agency.

tension_points.bull_case: Japan's Katayama is signalling coordinated action with the US Treasury against one-sided, rapid yen moves after USDJPY broke 160, and Tokyo has intervened several times this year.
tension_points.bear_case: UBS FX trading says the move is dollar-driven rather than yen-led, and the Fed is more hawkish than the BoJ with more hikes priced, so rate differentials would stay unchanged or widen and intervention would likely fail longer term.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A dovish turn at the Fed that narrows rate differentials.

tension_points.bull_case: Gold's Asia bounce and a possible dovish turn could reverse the market quickly, and silver has firmer physical support from ETF creation and the structural deficit.
tension_points.bear_case: Punitive real yields, elevated speculative length and ETF outflows leave gold tactically bearish below $3,940-4,000.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A dovish turn at the Fed, or gold holding above $3,940-4,000, would undercut the bearish setup.
